title: Worker Lab
thesis: Medir al worker completo: admisión, trabajo local, calidad, I/O, residencia, reallocation, recuperación y síntesis. Una métrica aislada no decide.
authority_boundary: Observability/learning only. Binding contracts, atomic claims, Work Graph and Design DNA remain authority.

confirmation.rationale: Both candidates cleared the full gate. V3 becomes the default baseline to avoid adding an untested unconditional second-pass overhead; V4 remains a confirmed optional reinforcement.

analysis_dimensions.title: Entrada y routing
analysis_dimensions.question: ¿Entró bien, obtuvo una sola autoridad y cuánto tardó en conseguir trabajo?
analysis_dimensions.improvement_goal: Entrar rápido, una sola vez, al trabajo correcto.

analysis_dimensions.title: Continuidad y recuperación
analysis_dimensions.question: ¿Conservó el trabajo, devolvió resultado, siguió o pudo recuperarse sin repetir?
analysis_dimensions.improvement_goal: No perder trabajo y continuar sin intervención humana innecesaria.

analysis_dimensions.title: Eficiencia y tiempo
analysis_dimensions.question: ¿Dónde se fue el tiempo y cuánto fue trabajo útil versus espera/I/O?
analysis_dimensions.improvement_goal: Maximizar trabajo útil por minuto y por operación externa.

analysis_dimensions.title: Capacidad local
analysis_dimensions.question: ¿Cuánto trabajo sostuvo este chat antes de terminar o degradarse?
analysis_dimensions.improvement_goal: Aumentar el trabajo útil por carga de contexto sin perder control.

analysis_dimensions.title: Calidad y retención
analysis_dimensions.question: ¿Mantuvo reglas, cobertura y calidad desde el principio hasta el final?
analysis_dimensions.improvement_goal: Escalar volumen sin perder precisión ni evidencia.

analysis_dimensions.title: Paralelismo y escala
analysis_dimensions.question: ¿Qué concurrencia lo rodeó y cómo cambió velocidad, calidad o fallos?
analysis_dimensions.improvement_goal: Encontrar el N que maximiza throughput útil, no sólo workers abiertos.

analysis_dimensions.title: Perfil de trabajo
analysis_dimensions.question: ¿Qué clase de trabajo hizo y cuál es su configuración óptima?
analysis_dimensions.improvement_goal: No asumir que una receta de worker sirve igual para todos los perfiles.

analysis_dimensions.title: Observabilidad y evidencia
analysis_dimensions.question: ¿Qué sabemos de verdad y qué sigue siendo UNKNOWN?
analysis_dimensions.improvement_goal: Poder reconstruir el worker de inicio a fin sin inventar cero ni liveness.

analysis_journal_schema.rule: Journal entries are candidate knowledge until independently promoted. Never store raw private chain-of-thought.

rules.hypothesis: A fresh shell needs externally durable identity before assignment so historical chat identity cannot masquerade as current execution.
rules.observed: The pipeline requires fresh worker_id + launch_nonce and beacon as the first durable write; the exam rejects historical identity for v3.30.
rules.when_not_to_use: Never reinterpret a prior worker_id/exam as a new launch.
rules.next_test: Keep identity invariant while varying later worker stages; verify every fresh launch remains reconstructible from beacon+nonce.

rules.hypothesis: A worker can do materially larger local blocks between external I/O boundaries without late-batch quality collapse.
rules.observed: Nine recovered replicas completed a heterogeneous local batch of roughly 2268-2548 output words with external_reads=0, external_writes=0, tool_calls=0, retries=0 and no reported late-batch degradation.
rules.when_to_use: Candidate guidance for grouping internally coherent local reasoning/transformation before the next necessary external read/write.
rules.when_not_to_use: Do not infer unlimited batch size, real elapsed speed, or safety of batching across mutable authority boundaries.
rules.next_test: Compare equal work split into many small I/O-separated blocks versus one larger local macro-batch using external durable timestamps and identical acceptance criteria.

rules.hypothesis: Performance claims should use external durable timestamps when available rather than model-authored clocks.
rules.observed: The recovered 10x experiment explicitly marks self-reported durations as diagnostic only; the pipeline timing contract prioritizes durable artifact timestamps.
rules.when_to_use: Latency, throughput, time-to-assignment, time-to-first-edit, time-to-return and reallocation measurements.
rules.when_not_to_use: Do not compare workers by self-reported start/end times as if they were trustworthy wall-clock telemetry.
rules.next_test: Instrument one canary with externally timestamped beacon, claim, first material write, verification and RETURN, then compare against self-reported timing.

rules.hypothesis: Telemetry should be sparse, reconstructive and non-authoritative so observability does not become worker overhead.
rules.observed: The event stream allows at most ROUTED, CLAIM_RESULT and CLOSE comments; missing telemetry cannot block allocation, work, RETURN or recovery.
rules.when_to_use: Lifecycle observability around real work, especially in POOL/BATCH.
rules.when_not_to_use: Do not emit heartbeat/event growth as a substitute for productive work or retry blocked telemetry.
rules.next_test: Measure useful durable work per GitHub write before and after coalescing non-authoritative lifecycle events.

rules.hypothesis: Execution authority must come from atomic unique assignment, not narrative state or optimistic local selection.
rules.observed: Pipeline E2 requires atomic slot/PIN assignment; reuse contract preserves deterministic sharding with atomic CREATE as authority.
rules.when_to_use: Every claimable work unit, including pool assignments and bounded RUN slots.
rules.when_not_to_use: Do not treat ACTIVE/PARKED/current_job_id, telemetry, or a selected candidate as ownership.
rules.next_test: Run controlled contention on one claim path and verify exactly one owner while losers reallocate without duplicate mutation.

rules.hypothesis: Concurrent POOL workers should distribute across compatible work using the fresh beacon commit SHA rather than restart identical traversal.
rules.observed: The reuse contract binds stable capability filtering and deterministic sharding from beacon_commit_sha with atomic CREATE as final authority.
rules.when_to_use: POOL/BATCH launches with multiple concurrently arriving workers.
rules.when_not_to_use: Do not locally invent a scheduler, priority system, or human-numbered routing layer.
rules.next_test: Launch a bounded cohort against a frozen compact frontier and measure collisions, assignment spread and productive starts per beacon.

rules.hypothesis: Useful chat capacity should continue after one completed unit instead of terminating immediately.
rules.observed: Current worker reuse and productivity exam both bind checkpoint=3 productive units, target=6, hard cap=8 unless a real boundary/exhaustion exists.
rules.when_to_use: v3.30 POOL workers after each counted durable RETURN.
rules.when_not_to_use: Do not continue through safety, authority, capability, transport, exhaustion, duplicate-ownership or runtime boundaries.
rules.next_test: Compare one-and-done workers with resident 3/6/8 chains on productive units per launch and time-to-reallocation.

rules.hypothesis: Fixed experiment runs and ordinary capacity need different routing semantics.
rules.observed: RUN is reserved for bounded frozen experiments/fixtures with explicit slots; POOL is normal ongoing generic capacity with no expected-count barrier.
rules.when_to_use: Choose RUN for reproducible experiments; use POOL for rolling productive work.
rules.when_not_to_use: Do not grow RUN packets into the general scheduler or impose cohort barriers on POOL.
rules.next_test: Confirm identical work demand behaves correctly under a frozen RUN packet and a rolling POOL without cross-contaminating authority semantics.

rules.hypothesis: Workers close more reliably when each acceptance gate is mapped to exact evidence before terminal status.
rules.observed: Pipeline E6 names V3_EVIDENCE_MAP as the promoted baseline and keeps DONE distinct from PASS.
rules.when_to_use: Any executable objective with hard gates.
rules.when_not_to_use: Do not claim verification that was not actually executed or convert BOUNDARY into PASS.
rules.next_test: For a matched job class, compare evidence-map-first closure with an otherwise identical control on missed gates and repair loops.

rules.hypothesis: Worker productivity should score durable useful outcomes, not verbosity or telemetry volume.
rules.observed: The productivity exam scores evidence-backed productive slots and explicitly excludes prose length, telemetry-only work, claims and heartbeats from productive credit.
rules.when_to_use: Worker comparison, experiment review and allocator diagnostics.
rules.when_not_to_use: Do not optimize for word count, commit count, heartbeat count or visible churn merely to raise a score.
rules.next_test: Track useful durable outputs per launch and per external write while holding acceptance quality constant.

negative_knowledge.consequence: Do not use the 56-432 second self-reported range as primary performance evidence.
Use durable external worker identity, not locally invented replica identity, for execution authority.
Persist recoverable work state; never imply an old chat shell is still alive.
Diagnose the weak pipeline stage before scaling launches.
Events may aid reconstruction but never create ownership or completion.
A v3.30 POOL worker below six productive units needs a durable allowed close reason.

Measure wake→beacon and beacon→claim separately. Oversubscription/replacement is valid for pre-authority admission loss, but do not count these workers in workload-quality denominators. Admission failure, not cognition/workload failure.

A worker that produced the workload but cannot persist RETURN is not equivalent to a worker that failed the workload. Preserve local-complete/durable-incomplete distinction. Useful local work may have succeeded while durable completion failed. Classify orchestration/transport separately from cognition.
Curiosity/verification can contaminate frozen experiments. Own-slot evidence must remain isolated until CLOSE; independent analyzer reads all slots later. Replica invalid for causal comparison.

Verification dimensions must stay separate. A missing browser check is not a workload failure unless browser verification is a declared hard gate. Do not downgrade local benchmark completion to failure; preserve browser/public verification as a separate boundary.

examples.chat_visible_reason: Attempted slot-claim CREATE was explicitly blocked by connector/security before authority. Worker did not skip to another slot or fabricate B1-B6 work.

timeline.title: ZIP / Root Dispatcher era
timeline.summary: Historical workflow used external chats as workers, the main chat as a Root Dispatcher, and the human as temporary transport for prompts/returns. Narrow missions and packaged ZIP/return artifacts were preferred over generic consultancy. The long-term intention was to automate the transport inside Prometeo.
timeline.lesson: Human copy/paste is a transitional transport, not the target architecture. Keep worker missions narrow and returns integrable.
timeline.evidence_boundary: Recovered project-history/file context; not proof of current runtime behavior.

timeline.title: Worker Evolution Lab
timeline.summary: CATLAB exploration used stage-specific variants and independent replicas. CATLAB-P2B confirmed V3_EVIDENCE_MAP and V4_TWO_PASS_REVIEW 3/3 each for primary+reallocation; V3 was promoted as baseline to avoid unconditional extra overhead.
timeline.lesson: Change one stage rule at a time; completion/evidence outrank speed. Reproduce candidate laws before promotion.

timeline.title: PARKED / early-exit failure mode
timeline.summary: Earlier SWARM-era flows explicitly returned PARKED/WAIT states and many shells stopped early. The human repeatedly observed that worker-visible terminal vocabulary made it easy for a shell to stop rather than continue useful work.
timeline.lesson: Do not use PARKED/ACTIVE as liveness. Present useful continuation as the normal path. Terminal language must correspond to a real durable boundary, not a convenient narrative exit.
timeline.evidence_boundary: The durable current law is strong; the claimed psychological wording effect remains a human observation until reproduced experimentally.

timeline.title: Large text batches kept workers producing
timeline.summary: Historical grid experiments suggested that workers could continue producing substantial local text batches when the task itself remained concrete, rather than entering wait/parking behavior.
timeline.lesson: Test local productive load as a residency tool, but do not confuse synthetic text with product value.
timeline.evidence_boundary: Historical reconstruction; exact receipts for the older grid figures remain incomplete.

timeline.title: LOCAL_CAPACITY_V2_10X
timeline.summary: Nine recovered replicas completed the heterogeneous local batch, each around 2268–2548 output words. Workers reported zero external tools/reads/writes and no late-batch degradation; timing remained self-reported only. Two distinct conversations produced the same model-generated replica_id.
timeline.lesson: Large local batches are promising; model-generated identity and self-reported clocks are not trustworthy authority.

timeline.title: Worker Playbook distilled
timeline.summary: Binding laws and experimental findings were distilled into a human+machine playbook covering fresh identity, local batching, external clocks, sparse writes, atomic ownership, deterministic sharding, resident 3/6/8, RUN vs POOL and evidence-map verification.
timeline.lesson: Worker learning must be written back, not left inside the Guide/chat.

timeline.title: Prerequisite gating bug
timeline.summary: PRE-GUIDE critic/finalizer jobs became claimable before prerequisites were satisfied. Internal job instructions returned dependency boundaries instead of fabricating results, but capacity was wasted.
timeline.lesson: Do not rely on the model to respect dependency order when the allocator can enforce it. Gate prerequisites below the worker interface.

timeline.title: System-multiplier starvation
timeline.summary: High-priority worker/runtime improvement jobs were READY but could be absent from the compact POOL frontier because product work filled the unified batch first.
timeline.lesson: Keep product dominant while reserving a tiny bounded share for system multipliers, otherwise orchestration fixes can starve indefinitely.

timeline.title: Explicit zero-ledger
timeline.summary: Writing or mentally holding expected external_reads=0/external_writes=0/tool_calls=0 may reinforce instruction retention, but it is not security and self-reported zeros are not external measurement.
timeline.lesson: Use zero-ledger as a prompting variant only; verify externally and never upgrade missing evidence to zero.

timeline.title: Block review / continuation priming / fill-the-questions
timeline.summary: Three candidate prompting techniques are under controlled comparison: silent review after each local block, explicit anti-early-answer continuation priming, and a PRE-GUIDE question scaffold that must be filled before return.
timeline.lesson: These are interventions, not laws. Compare matched replicas and preserve one causal delta per variant.

timeline.title: First 15 reported RUN launches produced no RUN evidence
timeline.summary: The human reported launching 15 chats, while durable RUN status still showed zero RUN beacons and zero slot claims. Causal attribution was unknown, so the system stopped scaling instead of pretending those launches entered the benchmark.
timeline.lesson: Human launch count is not slot occupancy. Admission must be measured from durable beacon+claim evidence.
timeline.evidence_boundary: 15 launch attempts came from human report; durable observation was zero RUN beacons/claims at that checkpoint.

timeline.title: Single RUN admission canary succeeded
timeline.summary: Fresh worker wc-20260930T102900Z-d4a7c91e52bf created a RUN beacon, claimed S002 (V1_EXPLICIT_ZERO_LEDGER), reached the single B3 MIDPOINT, completed the 72-task primary with 3636 useful words, persisted the primary receipt and claimed paired reallocation R002.
timeline.lesson: The previously unproven RUN admission path now works through primary return and entry into reallocation. The correct next move is parallel scale, not more sequential admission probing.

timeline.title: Admission canary must not freeze the broader lab
timeline.summary: A one-worker canary is appropriate when a previously broken transition is unproven. It should not pause unrelated parallel worker experiments, and once the failed transition is crossed, the frozen cohort should scale immediately.
timeline.lesson: Use sequential canaries for unknown failure boundaries, not as the default experimental cadence.
timeline.next_test: Run the remaining RESIDENCY-MACROBATCH slots in parallel and measure admission loss, variant completion, residency and reallocation.

open_questions: What macro-batch size maximizes useful work per external I/O before quality declines?
Which prompting variant improves completion/residency without increasing correction or evidence debt?
What is the externally observed distribution of claim→midpoint→primary→reallocation→close duration?
How much does wording change early termination independent of workload difficulty?
How many GitHub reads/writes occur per useful durable unit under macro-batching?
Can two independent worker analysts reliably prepare the Guide's human-facing answer?
What is the right admission-canary threshold before parallel scale for future RUNs?
What local macro-batch size maximizes useful work per external I/O without increasing correction rate or missed acceptance gates?
How much does sparse event/write coalescing reduce GitHub churn without harming reconstructability?
Does resident 3/6/8 materially improve productive units per human launch after accounting for reallocation collisions?
Are deterministic beacon-SHA shards balanced enough under real mixed capability frontiers?

law.externally_observed_wins: Externally observed counters must come from tool/transport/commit/workflow/artifact evidence. Model prose never upgrades UNKNOWN to a number.
law.zero_requires_closed_coverage: A numeric zero is valid only when coverage=COMPLETE_FOR_SCOPE and coverage_evidence_refs proves the observed external trace or bounded fixture is closed for that counter.
law.unknown_is_honest: When the runtime cannot reconstruct a complete external trace, use UNKNOWN plus unknown_reason; never infer zero from missing evidence.
law.wall_clock: External wall-clock is optional diagnostic telemetry only. Model-authored timestamps or duration guesses are not performance evidence.

coalescing.rule: Accumulate observable counters during the unit, then persist one compact measurement object. Existing ROUTED/STARTED/CLOSE and heartbeat mechanisms remain unchanged.

fail_when: numeric zero with coverage other than COMPLETE_FOR_SCOPE
model_self_reported value used as externally_observed evidence

recommended_measurements: useful output words/tasks per external write
next_program: Treat current_run as the newest durable launch packet, never a hardcoded historical benchmark.
Keep older RUNs in previous_runs for comparison without letting them drive current human action.
Reconcile durable stage failures with chat-visible final reasons.
Estimate provisional sustainable load separately for control and continuation priming.
If 30K passes, raise the ceiling rather than declaring 30K the maximum.
Run independent analysts over final receipts and write validated lessons back into Worker Playbook.
